decks.notes: This deck relies on quickly ramping up mana with Amulet of Vigor and bounce lands to cast Primeval Titan, fetching strong utility lands like The Mycosynth Gardens and Urza's Saga. By creating multiple land drops per turn and utilizing the unique abilities of each land, the deck can assemble a powerful engine to overwhelm the opponent with massive creatures and game-ending combos. The synergy between cards like Dryad of the Ilysian Grove and Cultivator Colossus further enhances the deck's ability to generate mana and create explosive plays.

The main focus of the deck is to control the game by using cards that disrupt the opponent's strategy, while also teaching the control player how to effectively manage resources and make decisions that will ultimately lead to victory. The deck includes cards that provide card selection, removal spells, and efficient creatures to apply pressure. The addition of Jegantha, the Wellspring as a companion adds an additional layer of strategy to the deck, requiring the player to adjust their deck construction while still maintaining the overall game plan of control.

This deck focuses on playing aggressive creatures and burn spells to quickly deal damage to the opponent. It utilizes a wide range of colors to maximize the power of Tribal Flames and Leyline of the Guildpact. The companion Jegantha, the Wellspring provides additional mana acceleration. The deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with efficient creatures like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Wild Nacatl, while also disrupting their game plan with counterspells like Stubborn Denial. The key strategy is to maintain pressure on the opponent while controlling the board with a mix of creatures and burn spells.

The main concept of this deck is to leverage the graveyard as a resource by cycling creatures like Street Wraith and Architects of Will to fill it up, then casting a Living End to bring them all back into play. The deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with powerful creatures and disrupt their game plan with cards like Force of Negation and Grief. The inclusion of cards like Subtlety and Ardent Plea adds versatility to the deck, allowing for additional control and card advantage. Ultimately, the goal is to set up a game-winning board state through the combo of cycling creatures and Living End.

This deck focuses on a fast and aggressive strategy, utilizing a mix of powerful creatures and efficient spells to overwhelm the opponent quickly. The inclusion of Jegantha as a companion allows for additional mana fixing and ramping. Tribal Flames and Leyline of the Guildpact are key cards that enable damage and protection, while Stubborn Denial provides valuable counterplay. Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Scion of Draco offer strong threats, with Territorial Kavu and Nishoba Brawler providing additional aggression. The mana base is carefully chosen to support the deck's color requirements for consistent and explosive gameplay.

The main concept of this deck is to quickly ramp up mana and play powerful land cards such as Primeval Titan and Valakut, the Molten Pinnacle. Arboreal Grazer and Dryad of the Ilysian Grove are used to help accelerate mana production. The deck also utilizes cards like Amulet of Vigor to untap lands and generate even more mana. With the ability to search for key lands with cards like Expedition Map and Tolaria West, the deck aims to assemble powerful combinations to overwhelm the opponent with large creatures and powerful land effects.

This deck focuses on aggressive plays and disruption, using a combination of efficient creatures like Tarmogoyf and Dauthi Voidwalker, along with disruptive spells like Thoughtseize and Maelstrom Pulse. The goal is to apply pressure on the opponent while disrupting their game plan. Grist, the Hunger Tide can provide a constant stream of threats, while Sorin, Imperious Bloodlord can help buff your creatures and provide additional value. The deck's mana base is designed to support its aggressive game plan while also providing flexibility for its disruptive spells.

The deck focuses on quickly playing creatures like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Dragon's Rage Channeler to apply early pressure on the opponent. It utilizes counterspells like Spell Pierce and Counterspell to protect its threats and disrupt the opponent's strategy. The deck also includes cards like Unholy Heat and Lightning Bolt to efficiently remove opposing creatures. Additionally, the inclusion of Murktide Regent provides a powerful evasive threat to close out the game. The deck aims to win the game by maintaining a steady stream of threats while controlling the board with efficient removal and countermagic.

This deck focuses on aggressive plays using low-cost creatures like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Murktide Regent, backed up by efficient removal like Lightning Bolt and Unholy Heat. Counterspells provide protection while cantrips like Preordain and Expressive Iteration help with card selection. The deck aims to apply pressure early on and disrupt the opponent's game plan with tempo plays, using a mix of damage, card advantage, and counter magic to control the battlefield. The mana base is optimized to ensure consistent access to both red and blue spells.

This deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with aggressive creatures and disruptive spells, while also utilizing powerful card advantage engines like Dauthi Voidwalker and Grief. By efficiently removing threats with cards like Terminate and Thoughtseize, as well as pressuring the opponent with creatures like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse, this deck seeks to quickly close out the game before the opponent can stabilize. Blood Moon and Molten Collapse can also disrupt the opponent's mana base, further cementing this deck's aggressive game plan.

The main concept of this deck is to use a combination of removal spells and disruption to control the game, while also taking advantage of powerful creatures and artifacts. The deck focuses on preventing the opponent from developing their board, utilizing cards like Fatal Push, Thoughtseize, and Damnation. The inclusion of cards like Cabal Coffers and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth allows for ramping up mana to cast big threats like Karn, the Great Creator and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse. Overall, the strategy is to outvalue the opponent and win through attrition.

The main focus of this deck is to apply continuous pressure on the opponent by deploying disruptive creatures like Dauthi Voidwalker and Grief, while also controlling the game with cards like Liliana of the Veil and Thoughtseize. The deck also aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy with cards like Nihil Spellbomb and Pithing Needle, while using efficient removal spells like Fatal Push. The combination of hand disruption, creature pressure, and removal spells allows this deck to quickly dismantle the opponent's game plan and secure a victory through aggressive plays.

This deck focuses on quickly playing aggressive creatures and disrupting the opponent's strategy with discard spells. By combining powerful cards like Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer and Grief with disruptive cards like Thoughtseize and Angrath's Rampage, the deck aims to control the game while dealing damage to the opponent. The inclusion of powerful threats like Sheoldred, the Apocalypse and Kroxa, Titan of Death's Hunger adds to the deck's overall strategy of applying pressure and disrupting the opponent's game plan. Through a combination of early aggression and disruption, this deck aims to overwhelm the opponent and secure a quick victory.

This deck revolves around controlling the game through countering opponent's spells, removing threats, and utilizing The One Ring to manipulate the game in your favor. It focuses on card advantage and disruption, using powerful planeswalkers like Teferi, Time Raveler and Narset, Parter of Veils to control the board. With a mix of removal spells, counterspells, and card draw, the deck aims to outmaneuver opponents and secure victory through strategic plays and resource management. It combines control elements with card advantage to dominate the battlefield and dictate the pace of the game.

The main strategy of this Modern Control - UrzaTron deck is to assemble Urza's Mine, Urza's Power Plant, and Urza's Tower to generate a large amount of colorless mana quickly. The deck focuses on using this mana advantage to play powerful threats like Karn, the Great Creator, Wurmcoil Engine, and Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger. The deck also includes disruption like Oblivion Stone and All Is Dust to control the board and protect its powerful late-game threats. The goal is to outvalue and outlast opponents through mana advantage and powerful threats.

The main idea behind this UR Aggro deck is to apply early pressure on the opponent with efficient aggressive creatures like Dragon's Rage Channeler, Ragavan, and Murktide Regent, while disrupting their game plan with countermagic like Spell Pierce, Counterspell, and Subtlety. The deck aims to control the tempo of the game through a mix of card advantage with Mishra's Bauble and Expressive Iteration, removal spells like Lightning Bolt and Unholy Heat, and efficient cantrips like Preordain and Consider. Its goal is to close out the game quickly before the opponent can stabilize.
